metaDescription: Free online CSS Minifier. Compress your CSS code by removing whitespace and comments to improve website rendering speed and performance.
intro: Heavy stylesheets slowing down your site? Our free CSS Minifier instantly compresses your cascading style sheets, stripping out bloated formatting to deliver lightning-fast load times.
whatIs: The CSS Minifier is a performance optimization tool for web developers. It reduces the size of CSS files by aggressively removing all unnecessary characters, such as spaces, line breaks, indentation, and developer comments.
howToUse: Paste your beautifully formatted CSS code into the input field.
The tool outputs a single, continuous string of compressed CSS.
Copy the result to use in your production `.min.css` file.
howItWorks: The minifier engine parses the stylesheet and executes a series of safe deletions. It removes block comments `/* comment */`, strips spaces around colons `:` and brackets `{ }`, and removes the final semicolon `;` in a declaration block.
resultInterpretation: The output is mathematically identical to the browser but significantly smaller in bytes. This prevents CSS from 'render-blocking' your webpage for longer than necessary.
useCases: Production Builds: Generating the final `style.min.css` file for a custom WordPress theme.
Performance Audits: Fixing 'Eliminate render-blocking resources' warnings in Google Lighthouse.
Code Obfuscation: Making it slightly more difficult for competitors to easily read and copy your custom animations or design systems.
tipsAndLimitations: Keep a 'src' folder with your un-minified CSS for development, and only minify when you are ready to publish.
Advanced CSS features like `calc()` rely heavily on spaces (e.g., `calc(100% - 20px)`). Our tool safely preserves these required spaces while removing others.

faq.question: Can I un-minify CSS later?
faq.answer: Yes, you can run minified CSS through a 'CSS Formatter' or 'Beautifier' to add the spaces and line breaks back in, though you cannot recover any deleted developer comments.

faq.question: Does CSS minification actually matter?
faq.answer: Absolutely. On large websites, CSS files can be hundreds of kilobytes. Minifying them saves bandwidth, speeds up mobile loading, and directly improves SEO rankings.

disclaimer: Tool performs safe syntax minification. Ensure you do not accidentally minify CSS containing invalid syntax, as it may break the entire stylesheet.
